claims.statement: For a fixed finite directed graph, incidence B, edge vector w, any potential u and circulation q with B^T q=0 and |q_e|<=1 satisfy q dot w<=sum_e|w_e-(Bu)_e|. Equality of feasible primal and dual values certifies the displayed L1 minimum. This classical bound is the useful graph foundation, not a general natural-language or higher-degree guarantee.
dependencies: Fixed finite graph and declared incidence convention
Feasible potential and dual circulation with unit box bounds
claims.limits: Direct weak-duality argument: q dot w=q dot(w-Bu), bounded termwise by absolute residual. No new native host validation or proof of every adapter here.

claims.statement: For every integer k, -k and k have the same parity, so (-1)^(-k)=(-1)^k. Therefore swapping the two nonnegative counts cannot be a sign-reversing involution for the appendix sign formula.
dependencies: The sign formula and swap map stated by the manuscript
claims.limits: Refutes that stated cancellation mechanism, not every possible meron representation or unrelated exact gauge certificate.

findings.statement: The appendix claims sigma=(-1)^(Nplus-Nminus) changes from negative to positive when the counts swap. For k=Nplus-Nminus, swapping gives -k, the same parity; (1,0) and(0,1) both have sign-1. Thus the proposed involution does not cancel equal-weight odd sectors. The SU2 subsection repeats the unsupported implication. This is a direct algebraic contradiction in TeX and PDF, irrespective of receipt status.
findings.recommended_action: Retain as a negative control; withdraw the cancellation/physical sign claim until an actually sign-reversing, weight-preserving involution is specified and checked. Do not repair historical receipts to mask the contradiction.
